reviews.author: Kyungmin Kim
reviews.text:
This is a place where you can enjoy LPs using a turntable.

Instructions for using the turntable were written on the desk and included in a booklet, so there wasn't anything too difficult.

There are a ton of different types of LPs, but they are not properly categorized, so it is virtually impossible to find the album you want.
There are about 100 albums recommended here, and you have to choose from them and listen to them. I was disappointed that I couldn't find the album I wanted to listen to.

The drinks were a bit expensive compared to the quality, but considering it was the cost of listening to LPs, it wasn't unreasonable.

In addition to the headsets provided at the store, I was also able to use my own earphones, as listening to music is my hobby.
If you have good earphones, use your own.
It's good. I didn't like the one provided as standard because the sound quality was poor and there was noise due to frequent use.

What was a little disappointing was that I went there to listen to music, but the music was played quite loudly in the store as well.
It was a pity that it interrupted my enjoyment of the music.

There weren't many places where you could use turntables, and the atmosphere inside the store was good, so there were some disappointments.
It was nice to spend time with my friend.

I recommend it to anyone who seriously enjoys music.
I think people who want to have fun while listening to music casually will be quite satisfied.

A must-visit place in Seoul! This is my favorite place in Seoul. I stayed there for two weeks and stopped by almost every day!!!

The oat milk latte was really great! The texture and taste of oat milk was the best I've ever had in my life (I'm on a dairy-free diet, so take my word for it!). Plus, the coffee flavor was strong enough to go perfectly with the oat milk, so it was really delicious 🤌🏾

I was disappointed that there wasn't a delicious dessert, but on the last day, I surprisingly found out that there were three options. It was absolutely perfect!

The Basque cheesecake was the best I've had in Seoul. Texture, balanced taste... It was absolutely perfect!! And chocolate brownies… oh my god! I finally found a brownie in Seoul, and it was the best brownie I've ever had.

And lastly, our team members are really friendly and always ready to help you, smile and chat even if their English isn't fluent. And there is a cute cat named Ott living here, so if you go, be sure to say hello and pet it! 😻

OOF team, thank you for everything. If I go to Seoul again, I will definitely come back and say hello!!

reviews.author: Bungeoppang Boy (Bunggeoppang Boy)
reviews.text:
A tea house specializing in tea located near Anguk Station. Located about 10-15 minutes from the station. Waiting was possible through the app, so it was more convenient if you visited at the reserved time.

When I went up to the second floor, it wasn't large and the seats weren't very spaced apart. There were cups and dishes displayed on the wall that seemed to be sold separately. Once I sat down at the prepared seat, a menu was brought to me, and I had to go to the counter to order the menu I chose.

The prepared menu came out right away, and when I ordered oolong tea, they told me how to brew it and drink it. I ordered the famous dessert, lemon jelly and ice cream cake. I also ordered a milk tea menu.

The tea was delicious and the third time I brewed it, the scent was subtle and went well. The milk tea looked good, but it was too sweet and not for my taste. The lemon jelly looked very pretty and that was the end of it. The ice cream cake was delicious.

The disappointing part is that the price was not reasonable. First of all, the prices of all desserts, including tea, were high. Since you have to make the tee yourself, the price was very disappointing if it did not include the cost of paying for the service.

Additionally, the space was small and the spacing between seats was narrow, so it did not fit the concept of a tea-based teahouse. It was a very difficult environment to drink the tea that I brewed slowly because the conversation around me was so loud and it was thick. I don't know if there is a time limit, but if it were, I felt like I would feel that way more, so it was a big disappointment.

The owner personally serves the food and even asks how it tastes, he is not arrogant at all. However, the menu selection is limited, the appetizers are average, and the service is a bit slow. The atmosphere is a bit old, but it gives it a comfortable, old-fashioned feel. If you come expecting food, you might be disappointed, but if you want to quietly relax and listen to old pop music, this is a hidden gem. It gets quite crowded after 8pm, so it's best to go early to get a good spot.

It's better to go for the second round rather than the first, and it's a good place to go and have a drink while chewing on dried fish when you're full in Jongno 3-ga.
